paragraphs: In Berakhot 60a he walks behind Rav Hamnuna and sighs. Rav Hamnuna asks, “Do you want to bring suffering upon yourself? It is written, ‘What I feared…’” Yehudah asks, “But isn’t it written, ‘Happy is the person who always fears’?” Rav Hamnuna replies that the verse refers to matters of Torah. Hyman cites the Dikdukei Soferim reading: R' Yehudah, son of R' Natan, was walking באתריה of Rabbi in the market of Tiberias, etc.

notes.text: The ordinary Berakhot paragraph has Yehudah sighing and Rav Hamnuna replying. The cited alternate wording באתריה may mean in Rabbi’s locale or reflect בתריה, behind him; that wording remains unresolved.

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier Berakhot consultation is inherited, not claimed newly read: Yehudah sighs and Rav Hamnuna replies, superseding the older reversed subject. שקיל in the attributed Dikdukei Soferim variant describes walking, not weighing goods; באתריה could mean in Rabbi's locale or reflect בתריה, behind, and remains explicit. The variant's Yehudah/Natan title abbreviations remain R', whereas final רבי is full Rabbi without an added name. The verse fragments and final etc. remain abbreviated; no new collation or genealogical identity is asserted.

The consulted Dikdukei Soferim (Berakhot, p. 342) has באתריה דרבי בשוקא דטבריא in the manuscript column. The corresponding print column has בתריה דרב המנונא, the reading in the standard Berakhot passage. The first wording places the episode in Rabbi's locale, in the market of Tiberias; the text cited here does not specify Rabbi's identity.
